whyItMatters: Hierarchy expressed only by size collapses once a user sets their own text size - and it was never available to screen reader users in the first place.

title: Media Alternatives Controllable
summary: The viewer, not the page, decides whether closed captions and audio descriptions are playing, and can change that at any point.
whyItMatters: Which alternative helps depends on the viewer. Control is what lets people sharing a screen, or with different needs, use the same media.

title: Media Alternatives Searchable
summary: Alternatives for media - transcripts and the like - can be searched and queried.
whyItMatters: Search is what makes a long transcript usable for finding one fact, rather than a wall of text to read through.

title: Media Chapters Available
summary: Audio or video of five minutes or longer can be navigated by chapters, unless it is a piece of music the composer did not divide into movements.
whyItMatters: Scrubbing a timeline precisely is difficult with a switch, a head pointer or a tremor. Chapters give structural navigation that does not depend on fine pointer control.

title: Page/view audio adjustable
summary: Where audio plays automatically, users can pause it, stop it, and adjust its volume separately from the system volume. All three are required, which is stricter than WCAG 2.2's 1.4.2, where any one of them is enough.
whyItMatters: Background audio masks a screen reader's speech, making the page unusable until it stops - and the system volume control turns off both at once.
